title: Trains to Eastbourne
lead: These are the trains I would look at for Airbourne. Southern runs a train from London Victoria to Eastbourne every half an hour, through Clapham Junction, East Croydon and Gatwick, and the coast trains bring you in from Brighton and Hastings. I’ve added a few connections that work well too, like Thameslink from St Pancras with a quick change at East Croydon. If you’re starting on the c2c line, from Shoeburyness, Southend, Basildon, Grays or anywhere along to Barking, I’ve added those stations too, with the change in London. Pick your station, a day and a time below and the map shows every station on the way.
facts: Every day, all four show days
Every 30 minutes from London, hourly on Sundays
ysIntro: This is the station I would get off at for Airbourne. The details below follow the train you pick further down the page.
walkLine: From the station it’s about 10 to 15 minutes on foot. Head down through the town centre to the seafront, then walk west along the prom to the Western Lawns by the Wish Tower. On show days there are plenty of stewards and signs, and you can just follow the crowd.
walkBack: Allow about 15 minutes to walk back up to the station from the Western Lawns, and a bit more when the crowds leave.
note: Due to how complicated the rail network is, this page only shows trains run by Southern, plus the Thameslink and Gatwick Express trains that connect with them, and South Western Railway from London Waterloo to Clapham Junction. Times are from the National Rail timetable for Thursday 5 to Sunday 8 November 2026, checked on 30 October 2026. The big stations and city termini further from Eastbourne use the times for Friday 13, Saturday 14 and Sunday 15 November 2026, checked on 10 November 2026. Times for summer 2027 usually come out in the spring, so please check with Southern before you travel. The line is drawn along the railway, so treat it as a guide. gaOnly: Southern trains, plus a few connections. Due to how complicated the rail network is, I only show Southern trains into Eastbourne, plus the Thameslink and Gatwick Express trains that connect well with them, as they’re all run by the same company. From Waterloo I’ve added the short hop on South Western Railway to Clapham Junction, where you change onto Southern. If you’re coming from further away, I would plan your trip to one of these stations first and pick it up from there. I’ve also added eight c2c stations, with the c2c train into London and the connection on from there.

x.tipArrive: The seafront fills up early, especially at the weekend, so I would get there before the showground opens. If you want a front row seat, head there first and save your pitch. Then take a look round the RAF Village, speak to the crews, visit the trade stalls and check the food options. Visit the toilet before the flying display starts.

text: A lot of the journeys on this page change at Brighton, especially from Portsmouth and along the coast, and some of the London trains do too. When I last checked, the change there was usually about {typ} minutes, and anything from {min} to {max} minutes depending on the train.

Brighton is the end of the line, so you walk back down the platform to the concourse. I would find your next train on the boards straight away and keep an eye on them, as platforms can change on the day.

Coming home, I would give yourself more time than you think you need. The trains out of Eastbourne are packed straight after the flying, and if yours runs a few minutes late you could end up waiting at Brighton for the next one.

x.busyTip: The trains home are busiest straight after the flying display ends, as everyone walks up to the station at once. I would advise waiting a bit and grabbing something to eat in town. If you aren’t waiting to see the last display, leaving before it starts may work for you too. Your last train time is just below, so check it before you settle in.

about.London Victoria|Clapham Junction: Out over the Thames on Grosvenor Bridge, right by Battersea Power Station.
about.Clapham Junction|East Croydon: Through the south London suburbs, past Balham and Streatham Common.
about.London Bridge|East Croydon: Out past the Shard and through the south London suburbs, with Norwood Junction just before Croydon.
about.London St Pancras|East Croydon: Under the City through Farringdon, across the Thames at Blackfriars, then out through London Bridge and the south London suburbs.
about.East Croydon|Gatwick Airport: Over the North Downs and through the Merstham tunnels. Keep an eye out for aircraft as you come into Gatwick.
about.Gatwick Airport|Haywards Heath: Past Three Bridges and across the Ouse Valley Viaduct, just after Balcombe. It’s one of the finest bits of Victorian railway in the country, so it’s worth looking out of the window.
about.Three Bridges|Haywards Heath: Through Balcombe and across the Ouse Valley Viaduct, one of the finest bits of Victorian railway in the country.
about.Haywards Heath|Lewes: Off the main line just after Wivelsfield, then across the Sussex countryside under the South Downs.
about.Lewes|Polegate: Along the foot of the South Downs, past Glynde and Berwick.
about.Lewes|Eastbourne: Along the foot of the South Downs, past Glynde and Berwick, then through Polegate and Hampden Park into Eastbourne.
about.Polegate|Eastbourne: The last few minutes in, through Hampden Park. Eastbourne station sits at the end of a short branch, so trains carrying on to Hastings head back out the way they came.
about.Brighton|Lewes: Out through London Road, past the Amex Stadium at Falmer and under the South Downs to Lewes.
about.Hastings|Eastbourne: Along the coast through St Leonards and Bexhill, then across the Pevensey Levels, near where William the Conqueror landed in 1066.
about.Hastings|Polegate: Along the coast through St Leonards and Bexhill, then across the Pevensey Levels, near where William the Conqueror landed in 1066.

pay: An Advance ticket is often the cheapest way to go, but it ties you to one train. I would pick the train you want first, then book. They can sell out at the weekend, so I would book as soon as the summer times are out.
Think about an off peak ticket
An off peak ticket lets you choose the train on the day, which suits a show when you don’t know when you’ll want to go home. Check the time rules on the ticket before you buy.

A Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares, and it can pay for itself in one trip. Two Together, Senior, 16 to 25, 26 to 30 and Disabled Persons railcards all give a third off.
faq: Which station is closest to the show?

Eastbourne. It’s about a 10 to 15 minute walk down through the town to the seafront, and the Western Lawns are at the western end, by the Wish Tower. Hampden Park is on the way in, but it’s a good bit further out, so I would stay on to Eastbourne.
Do I need a ticket for the show?
No. Airbourne is free to watch, so it’s only the train fare to think about.
Thursday 12 to Sunday 15 August 2027. The times on this page are from this winter’s timetable, so treat them as a guide until the summer 2027 times come out.
Will there be extra trains on show days?
When I last checked, nothing had been announced for 2027. Southern usually runs longer trains on show days, so please check nearer the time.
What if my train is late or cancelled?

Take a look at the live board above or the National Rail app before you leave the house. On a flexible ticket you can usually take the next train. With an Advance ticket, speak to the staff at the station.
I’m coming from further away. What do I do?

I would plan your trip to whichever of the thirteen stations on this page is nearest to you, and pick it up from there. If you’re coming from Kent, Southeastern also runs trains to Hastings, which I have left off this page, so have a look at those too.
